questions.stem: The National Emblem of India is an adaptation of which ancient sculpture?

options.option_text: The Nataraja of the Chola period
The Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath
The Kailasa temple sculpture at Ellora

questions.explanation: The National Emblem of India is based on the LION CAPITAL OF ASHOKA at Sarnath (UP) — a sculpture atop an Ashokan pillar (~250 BCE) commemorating Buddha's first sermon. The original capital shows FOUR ADDORSED LIONS standing on an abacus (carrying four animals — lion, elephant, galloping horse, bull — separated by chakras), all on an inverted lotus. In the emblem, only 3 lions are visible (4th is hidden behind). Motto: 'SATYAMEVA JAYATE' (Truth alone triumphs) from the Mundaka Upanishad (not visible in the original sculpture — added to the emblem). Adopted on 26 January 1950. The original Sarnath sculpture is housed in the Sarnath Museum. A much larger recreation was installed atop the new Parliament building in July 2022.

questions.stem: The Indian National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was composed by Rabindranath Tagore. In which year was it officially adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.explanation: 'Jana Gana Mana' — written by Rabindranath Tagore originally in Bengali (titled 'Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata', 1911); first sung at INC's Calcutta session on 27 December 1911 — was officially adopted as the NATIONAL ANTHEM by the Constituent Assembly on 24 JANUARY 1950 (two days before the Constitution came into force). Full anthem: 5 stanzas; only the FIRST stanza is the national anthem. Duration: 52 seconds (full) or 20 seconds (short version). Composition tune: 'Raga Alhaiya Bilawal'. Same author also wrote Bangladesh's national anthem 'Amar Shonar Bangla' (1906). India's NATIONAL SONG 'Vande Mataram' (from Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath 1882) — also adopted 24 Jan 1950 with EQUAL status to the anthem — famously sung at 1896 Calcutta INC session by Tagore himself.

questions.stem: Who designed the Indian National Flag (its final 3-colour horizontal tricolour form adopted in 1947)?
questions.explanation: PINGALI VENKAYYA (1876-1963, Andhra Pradesh) — an Indian freedom fighter, agriculturist, and Gandhian — designed the basic pattern of the Indian national flag. The final tricolour (saffron-white-green with the Ashoka Chakra in navy blue at centre) was ADOPTED on 22 JULY 1947 by the Constituent Assembly. Earlier flag versions: MADAM BHIKAJI CAMA unfurled an early tricolour on 22 Aug 1907 at Stuttgart (Germany, Intl Socialist Congress) — 1st 'Indian' flag on foreign soil. Gandhi's 1921 design had red (later saffron), white, green with a charkha. Nandalal Bose — illustrator of the Constitution's manuscript. Colour meanings: Saffron = courage/sacrifice; White = peace/truth; Green = faith/fertility; Chakra = Dharma/motion. Ratio 2:3. BIS standard for hand-spun khadi only.

questions.explanation: GANGETIC RIVER DOLPHIN (Platanista gangetica, locally 'Susu' / 'Soons' in Bihar) was declared India's National Aquatic Animal on 5 October 2009 by PM Dr. Manmohan Singh. Found in Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna-Karnaphuli river systems. Endangered (IUCN). Blind — navigates via echolocation. Population ~3500. Project Dolphin launched 2020 (like Project Tiger). Full set of Indian national symbols (remember at least 13): FLAG, EMBLEM, ANTHEM, SONG, ANIMAL = Bengal Tiger (declared 1972), HERITAGE ANIMAL = Indian Elephant (2010), BIRD = Indian Peafowl (1963), AQUATIC ANIMAL = Gangetic Dolphin (2009), REPTILE = King Cobra, FLOWER = Lotus, TREE = Banyan, FRUIT = Mango, RIVER = Ganga (declared 2008), CURRENCY SYMBOL ₹ (Udaya Kumar, adopted 2010), CALENDAR = Saka Samvat (from 22 March 1957).

questions.stem: Who designed the Indian rupee symbol '₹', and in which year was it officially adopted by the Government of India?
questions.explanation: D. UDAYA KUMAR (IIT Guwahati faculty member, native of Kallakurichi TN) designed the rupee symbol '₹' — selected from ~3000 entries in a 2009 competition. Officially adopted on 15 JULY 2010 by the Union Cabinet. The symbol combines Devanagari 'र' (Ra) and Roman capital 'R' without the vertical line — featuring two parallel horizontal strokes on top (signifying India's tricolour or the '=' of equality). Before 2010, India used 'Rs.' Unicode code point U+20B9. India joined other major currencies with symbols: $ USD, € Euro, £ GBP, ¥ Yen, ₩ Won, ₹ Rupee (Sri Lanka and Nepal use their own). Thousand-separator: Indian system uses lakhs/crores (1,00,000 = 1 lakh, 10,00,00,000 = 10 crore); the Western system uses thousands/millions.

questions.stem: India's National Calendar is based on which calendar, effective since 22 March 1957?
questions.explanation: India's NATIONAL CALENDAR is the SAKA CALENDAR (Saka Samvat), adopted on 22 March 1957 based on the Calendar Reform Committee report (1952, chaired by Meghnad Saha). Year 1 of Saka era = 78 CE (commemorating Kanishka's coronation per one theory). First month = CHAITRA (starts 22 March, 21 March in leap year). Second month = VAISHAKHA, etc. Used officially for Gazette, AIR broadcasts, official calendars, some government communications. Current year: Saka 1946/47 (depending on month in 2024-25). Other Indian calendars: VIKRAM SAMVAT (year 1 = 57 BCE, still popular in Hindu tradition, 57 years ahead of CE), KALIYUGA era (3102 BCE start), Bengali calendar (Bongabdo), Tamil calendar, Malayalam (Kollam era), Saka-Kaliyug. International standards: Gregorian (civil/official), ISO 8601.

questions.stem: When was the Ganga declared India's National River, and during which anniversary was the declaration?
questions.explanation: The GANGA was declared India's NATIONAL RIVER on 4 November 2008 by the Union Cabinet, led by PM Manmohan Singh — and on the same day, the National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA) was constituted under the Environment Protection Act 1986 to clean the river. Later, the NATIONAL MISSION FOR CLEAN GANGA (NMCG, 2011) and the broader NAMAMI GANGE programme (2014, ₹20,000 Cr initial allocation) have been key initiatives. The Ganga flows ~2525 km through 5 states: Uttarakhand (Bhagirathi from Gangotri Glacier + Alaknanda → union at Devprayag → 'Ganga' thereafter), UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB. Enters Bangladesh as Padma → Jamuna (Brahmaputra) → Meghna → Bay of Bengal. Ganga + Yamuna basin covers 25% of India's land and supports 40%+ of the population.
